title: bug: worktree-mode sh/ps1 twin drift in labels and diagnostics (recovery-checkpoint status, interrupted-gate CheckRun, hooked-commit reason, post-flight MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT)
description:
Filed by WT-19's whole-epic adversarial review (task-b1ca54f2716442be889a14623eb59983, step 7).

PROBLEM. There are four small sh/ps1 drifts in worktree mode, and parity-check's string families cannot see them. Each changes only a label, a diagnostic or an evidence row. None moves a branch, and none records a false pass.
(a) On a fresh claim, sh labels a recovery checkpoint status=UNKNOWN.
(b) ps1 records no infra-failure CheckRun for an interrupted worktree-mode gate.
(c) sh misreports why a hooked commit's sparse helper failed.
(d) No landing post-flight prints MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT, which design §1.6 requires.

EVIDENCE. Checked on merged tree 88e507e5, which is moe/work-2026-10-24 at 1558f141 plus the WT-19 task.
(a) scripts/moe-agent.sh:10512 calls worktree_preflight with "${RESUME_TASK_STATUS:-}", which is empty unless the session is a resume. So sh:7868 sets LAND_STATUS="${3:-UNKNOWN}". scripts/moe-agent.ps1:9789-9791 passes the preflight context's task.status instead.
(b) The sh EXIT trap (sh:269) calls finish_gate_observation (sh:5890-5897), which records any gate that started but was never recorded as infra-failure. ps1 does that only in the shared landing's finally (ps1:6216-6230). In worktree mode:
- Invoke-MoeWorktreeCompletion's catch/finally (ps1:7264-7271) only warns and releases the lease;
- the outer finally (ps1:11188) only stops the gate child.
(c) The sh hooked-commit worktree arm empties private_git when sparse-checkout or read-tree fails (sh:5484-5487). The signing-config comparison then runs with GIT_DIR='' and writes 'hooked-commit-config-mismatch' (sh:5514-5515). ps1 throws 'hooked-commit-worktree-failed' (ps1:5048-5050).
(d) docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md:69 says "A post-flight that finds it still lands ... and prints the code". The only emitters are:
- pre-flight: sh:3439, ps1:3317;
- removal: sh:8199 and :8248, ps1:7726 and :7782;
- the sweep: sh:8405, ps1:7931.

IMPACT.
(a) The same recovery gets a different commit subject and ledger status on each engine.
(b) On Windows the ledger loses the interrupted gate attempt. No landing happens, but the rail-1 audit gets harder.
(c) An operator chases a signing mismatch that does not exist.
(d) A W that grew .moe is reported only at the next pre-flight.

FIX DIRECTION. Mirror whichever twin is right:
(a) sh passes the preflight context's task status.
(b) ps1 records the infra-failure CheckRun in the worktree completion's finally, or in the outer finally, when MoeGate.Started is set and MoeGate.Recorded is not.
(c) sh writes 'hooked-commit-worktree-failed' and returns when the sparse helper fails.
(d) Both landing post-flights check W/.moe, print MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT, and still land, as §1.6 says.
definitionOfDone: On a fresh claim, sh labels a worktree recovery checkpoint with the task's real status, as ps1 does.
ps1 records an infra-failure CheckRun for an interrupted worktree-mode gate on the exit paths sh's finish_gate_observation covers.
When the hooked-commit sparse-checkout/read-tree helper fails, both twins report 'hooked-commit-worktree-failed'.
Both landing post-flights print MOE_WORKTREE_MOE_PRESENT when W/.moe exists and still land, per design §1.6.
parity-check.sh/.ps1, worktree-landing.sh/.ps1 and postflight-safe (bash and powershell) all pass.
